mission.heading: Wonderland, Stopped
paragraphs: Wonderland stopped at six o'clock. Every clock shows the same hour, and the Looking-Glass at the heart of the land has cracked. Its Twisted Rules have flipped the world upside down.
You are Ellis, a clockmaker's apprentice who fell down a rabbit hole chasing a late White Rabbit.
Reach the Court of Hearts and restart time within ten minutes, with the Cheshire Cat at your side.

tutorial.text: Drag to look around the room. Pinch or scroll to zoom.
Tap glowing things to find, read or open them.
The Book keeps your tools, notes and Twisted Rules.
The X closes any panel. Pause stops the clock.
Wits are your score. Hints cost 25 Wits and you get 3 in the whole game. Wrong answers cost 10. You have 10:00.

rooms.name: Hall of Falling Clocks
rooms.objective: Open the great door of the Hall.
rooms.twistedRule: Clocks count the wrong way. The minute wheel turns 12 times for one turn of the hour wheel.

rooms.name: Drink-Me Pantry
rooms.twistedRuleTitle: Small is big, big is small
rooms.twistedRule: Small is big, big is small. Trust the number, not the glass.

rooms.name: The Mad Tea Party
rooms.objective: Seat the guests so tea can end.
rooms.twistedRule: It is always six o'clock. Guests sit by the six house rules.

rooms.name: Mushroom Glade
rooms.twistedRule: Answers come as questions. The Caterpillar speaks only in questions.

rooms.name: Looking Wood
rooms.objective: Light the way to the Looking-Glass gate.
rooms.twistedRule: Light goes where it likes. Living mirrors bend the beam.

rooms.name: Croquet Garden
rooms.objective: Cross the Queen's lawn to the heart gate.
rooms.twistedRule: Left is right. Every sign says left and means right.

rooms.name: Court of Hearts
rooms.objective: Restart time in the Court of Hearts.
rooms.twistedRule: Sentence first, verdict after. The trial reads backward.

items.name: Gear Case
items.text: Six brass gears, all different sizes. They have 6, 8, 12, 16, 18 and 24 teeth.

items.name: Crank Handle
items.text: A crank handle, worn smooth. It fits the peg on the great door.

items.name: Small Vial
items.text: A small vial marked 5. It holds 5 measures.

items.name: Tall Vial
items.text: A tall vial marked 8. It holds 8 measures.

items.name: Name Cards
items.text: Six place cards for the table: Hatter, March Hare, Dormouse, White Rabbit, Dodo and Duchess.

items.name: House Rules
items.text: Rules 1 to 3: the Hatter sits in seat 1. The March Hare sits in the next seat, going clockwise. The Dormouse sits straight across from the Hatter.

items.name: Clue Slate
items.text: Five clues for a ladder: a great height, a story, a bathroom wall square, the sea's pull, neat, and very small.

items.name: Chalk
items.text: A stub of white chalk. Good for writing on the flat mushroom.

items.name: Silver Lantern
items.text: A silver lantern, still warm. It shines a beam of light.

items.name: Mirror Guide
items.text: A slash mirror / turns a beam: east goes north, north goes east, west goes south, south goes west. A backslash mirror \ turns it: east goes south, south goes east, west goes north, north goes west.

items.name: Flamingo Mallet
items.text: A flamingo, used as a mallet. Rude. It lets you walk on the lawn.

items.name: Poem Scroll
items.text: A poem about roses. It tells which colour bed to step on, one row at a time.

items.name: Clock Key
items.text: A heavy brass key. It opens the great clock case.

items.name: Verdict Slate
items.text: Pressing an hour card flips that hour and its next-door hours. Hours 1 and 12 have only one neighbour. Light all twelve.

hotspots.label: Wall clock
hotspots.title: The Wall Clock
hotspots.text: The numbers run 12, 11, 10 the wrong way round. In this hall the minute wheel turns 12 times for one turn of the hour wheel.

hotspots.label: Clock cabinet
hotspots.text: Six brass gears, all different sizes.

hotspots.label: Rabbit's desk
hotspots.text: A crank handle, worn smooth.

hotspots.label: Stopped clock
hotspots.title: A Stopped Clock
hotspots.view2: The scratches look like claw marks. Something climbed here.
hotspots.grinNote: Scratched from outside, by something that climbs.

hotspots.label: Rabbit's note
hotspots.title: The Rabbit's Note
hotspots.text: The door wheel is the hour wheel. It must turn once for each twelve crank turns.

hotspots.label: Tiny door
hotspots.title: The Tiny Door
hotspots.text: A small plate says: Fit for six measures only.

hotspots.label: Shelf
hotspots.text: A small vial marked 5.

hotspots.label: Shelf
hotspots.text: A tall vial marked 8.

hotspots.label: Drink-Me label
hotspots.title: The Drink-Me Label
hotspots.view1: A big paper label hangs on the jug.
hotspots.view2: A curly tail is drawn where the name should be. The writer signs with a tail.
hotspots.grinNote: The writer signs with a tail, not a name.

hotspots.label: Vial label
hotspots.title: The Vial Label
hotspots.text: Small looks big and big looks small. Trust the number, not the glass.

hotspots.label: Tablecloth
hotspots.text: Six place cards, all blank.

hotspots.label: Hat on the chair
hotspots.text: A scroll of tea table rules.

hotspots.label: House Rules scroll
hotspots.title: House Rules 1 to 3
hotspots.text: Rule 1: the Hatter sits in seat 1. Rule 2: the March Hare sits in the next seat, going clockwise. Rule 3: the Dormouse sits straight across from the Hatter.

hotspots.label: Dormouse's cup
hotspots.title: The Dormouse Mumbles
hotspots.text: Rule 4: the White Rabbit is not next to the March Hare. Rule 5: the Dodo is next to the Dormouse. Rule 6: the Duchess is not next to the Dormouse.

hotspots.label: Teapot steam
hotspots.title: The Teapot Steam
hotspots.view1: The steam looks like a grin.
hotspots.view2: The Hatter says a friend with a wide smile asked him to keep it six o'clock, for a game.
hotspots.grinNote: A friend asked the Hatter to keep it six, "for a game".

hotspots.label: Caterpillar
hotspots.title: The Caterpillar
hotspots.text: He only speaks in questions. Ask the right question back: the ladder on the flat mushroom goes from TALL to TINY.

hotspots.label: Stump slate
hotspots.text: Five clues for a ladder.

hotspots.label: Under a cap
hotspots.text: A stub of white chalk.

hotspots.label: Smoke
hotspots.title: The Smoke
hotspots.view1: The smoke spells a word in the air.
hotspots.view2: It says STAY. Who wants someone to stay?
hotspots.grinNote: The smoke says STAY. Who wants someone to stay?

hotspots.label: Mirror trees
hotspots.title: The Mirror Trees
hotspots.text: The leaves are tiny mirrors. In this wood, light goes where it likes, and living mirrors can be turned.

hotspots.label: Root hollow
hotspots.text: A silver lantern, still warm.

hotspots.label: Carved stone
hotspots.text: A card showing how mirrors turn light.

hotspots.label: Standing glass
hotspots.title: The Standing Glass
hotspots.view1: A big mirror in a gold frame.
hotspots.view2: It shows a wide grin, but no cat. Whose grin is it?
hotspots.grinNote: The glass shows a grin with no cat. Whose grin?

hotspots.label: Signposts
hotspots.title: The Signposts
hotspots.text: Every sign says LEFT, but the arrow points right. In this garden, left is right.

hotspots.label: Mallet stand
hotspots.text: A flamingo, used as a mallet. Rude.

hotspots.label: Card Gardener's pocket
hotspots.text: A poem about roses.

hotspots.label: The hedge
hotspots.title: The Hedge
hotspots.view1: A gap in the leaves shaped like a smile.
hotspots.view2: A smiling voice from this hedge gave the Queen all her strange rules.
hotspots.grinNote: The Queen's rules came from a smiling voice in the hedge.

hotspots.label: Knave's slate
hotspots.title: The Knave's Slate
hotspots.text: The slate says: sentence first, verdict after. In this court the trial reads backward.

hotspots.label: Under the throne
hotspots.text: A heavy brass key.

hotspots.label: Judge's bench
hotspots.text: The press rule is written here.

hotspots.label: Crack in the glass
hotspots.title: The Crack
hotspots.view1: A long crack runs across the Looking-Glass.
hotspots.view2: The crack is shaped like a wide smile.
hotspots.grinNote: A crack shaped like a wide smile.

open1.speaker: ellis
open1.text: A hole, a fall, and now every clock says six.

open2.speaker: cat
open2.text: Welcome, Ellis. Wonderland is a little twisted today.

open4.speaker: cat
open4.text: Each place has a rule that flipped. Learn it and the place gives way.

open6.speaker: cat
open6.text: The Court of Hearts. Ten minutes, I'd say. Shall we?

idle1.speaker: cat
idle1.text: Try turning around. Drag to look around.

idle2.speaker: cat
idle2.text: Something here wants a closer look.

r1_enter1.speaker: rabbit
r1_enter1.text: Late, late! The door will not open and the clocks will not move!

r1_enter3.speaker: cat
r1_enter3.text: And the numbers run backward. Charming.

r1_disc1.speaker: ellis
r1_disc1.text: A gear frame and a crank peg. It is just a clock.

r1_disc2.speaker: cat
r1_disc2.text: Gears like rules. Find the rule.

r1_wrong1.speaker: cat
r1_wrong1.text: Close. Count the teeth. Bigger gears turn slower.

r1_wrong2.speaker: cat
r1_wrong2.text: The door turns once for every twelve cranks. Check the Rabbit's note.

r1_wrong3.speaker: cat
r1_wrong3.text: One of your two gears is four times the other.

r1_hint.speaker: cat
r1_hint.text: Teeth tell you speed. Pair a big gear with a small one.

r1_hint2.speaker: cat
r1_hint2.text: Try the biggest gear first, then the smallest.

r1_right1.speaker: ellis
r1_right1.text: Twelve cranks, one door turn. Just like a clock.

r1_right2.speaker: cat
r1_right2.text: You read time the right way round. How rare.

r2_enter1.speaker: ellis
r2_enter1.text: Shelves of bottles, and a door the size of a mousehole.

r2_enter2.speaker: cat
r2_enter2.text: Drink the right amount and you fit. The wrong amount, and you will regret it.

r2_disc1.speaker: ellis
r2_disc1.text: Two vials, a jug and a drain. It is a measuring puzzle.

r2_disc2.speaker: cat
r2_disc2.text: Small is big here. Trust the numbers.

r2_wrong1.speaker: cat
r2_wrong1.text: Not six. Empty a vial and pour again.

r2_wrong2.speaker: cat
r2_wrong2.text: Fill the big vial, pour it into the small one, and see what is left.

r2_wrong3.speaker: cat
r2_wrong3.text: You may empty a vial into the drain between pours.

r2_hint.speaker: cat
r2_hint.text: Pour the big vial into the small one and look at what is left.

r2_hint2.speaker: cat
r2_hint2.text: Fill, pour, empty, pour, fill, pour. Six moves.

r2_right1.speaker: ellis
r2_right1.text: Six measures, exactly the size of the door.

r2_right2.speaker: cat
r2_right2.text: Small is big. Delicious, isn't it?

r3_enter1.speaker: hatter
r3_enter1.text: A friend with a wide smile asked us to keep it six o'clock. For a game!

r3_enter2.speaker: cat
r3_enter2.text: Tea? No, thank you. I never take sugar with a secret.

r3_disc1.speaker: ellis
r3_disc1.text: Six guests, six chairs, six rules.

r3_disc2.speaker: cat
r3_disc2.text: At this table, it is always six. Do not be late.

r3_wrong1.speaker: hatter
r3_wrong1.text: No, no! That puts someone beside the wrong neighbour.

r3_wrong2.speaker: cat
r3_wrong2.text: Start at the Hatter's chair and go around clockwise.

r3_wrong3.speaker: cat
r3_wrong3.text: Seat the Hare and the Dormouse first. The rest follow.

r3_hint.speaker: cat
r3_hint.text: The Hare and the Dormouse are fixed by the first three rules.

r3_hint2.speaker: cat
r3_hint2.text: Seats 3, 5 and 6 are left for the Dodo, Rabbit and Duchess. Use rules 4 to 6.

r3_right3.speaker: cat
r3_right3.text: It is always six o'clock. A lovely hour to leave.

r4_enter4.speaker: cat
r4_enter4.text: He only answers in questions. Do ask him back.

r4_disc1.speaker: ellis
r4_disc1.text: Start tall, end tiny, one letter at a time.

r4_wrong1.speaker: caterpillar
r4_wrong1.text: Is that one letter? Is that a word?

r4_wrong2.speaker: cat
r4_wrong2.text: Change only one letter each time, and match the clue.

r4_wrong3.speaker: cat
r4_wrong3.text: Read the clue again. Does your word fit it?

r4_hint.speaker: cat
r4_hint.text: The first rung is a story. TALL loses one letter and gains another.

r4_hint2.speaker: cat
r4_hint2.text: A story, a wall square, the sea's pull, then neat.

r4_right1.speaker: caterpillar
r4_right1.text: Is that who you are? Tiny?

r4_right2.speaker: ellis
r4_right2.text: Apparently so. The smoke is opening a path.

r4_right3.speaker: cat
r4_right3.text: He asked, you answered. Rare as a quiet clock.

r5_disc1.speaker: ellis
r5_disc1.text: A lantern, a gate and two stones that must glow.

r5_disc2.speaker: cat
r5_disc2.text: Light goes where it likes. Make it like where you like.

r5_wrong1.speaker: cat
r5_wrong1.text: The beam left by the wrong door. Follow it from the lantern.

r5_wrong2.speaker: cat
r5_wrong2.text: A stone stayed dark. Both Grin Stones must glow.

r5_wrong3.speaker: cat
r5_wrong3.text: Hedges swallow light. Keep the beam away from them.

r5_hint.speaker: cat
r5_hint.text: The two mirrors by the lantern send the beam east along row 6.

r5_hint2.speaker: cat
r5_hint2.text: The beam goes up the right side, back down column G, then loops to the gate on row 8.

r5_right1.speaker: ellis
r5_right1.text: The beam crossed itself and still found the gate.

r5_right2.speaker: cat
r5_right2.text: Lovely. Now, which of us does the glass flatter?

r6_enter1.speaker: queen
r6_enter1.text: Off with their... oh. A guest. Walk my garden wrong and I shall be cross!

r6_enter2.speaker: cat
r6_enter2.text: She says that to everyone. She means it about half the time.

r6_disc1.speaker: ellis
r6_disc1.text: Six beds to cross, one poem to follow.

r6_disc2.speaker: cat
r6_disc2.text: Mind the signs. Everyone does, and everyone is wrong.

r6_wrong1.speaker: gardener
r6_wrong1.text: Oh dear! That is a guard card bed!

r6_wrong2.speaker: cat
r6_wrong2.text: Check the colour of each bed against the poem, line by line.

r6_wrong3.speaker: cat
r6_wrong3.text: The poem's left is the garden's right.

r6_hint.speaker: cat
r6_hint.text: Left is right here. Turn right at the fourth bed.

r6_hint2.speaker: cat
r6_hint2.text: Start at the pink in the middle of the front row.

r6_right1.speaker: queen
r6_right1.text: How dare you walk it right! Carry on.

r6_right3.speaker: cat
r6_right3.text: A clever rule, whoever made it.

r7_enter1.speaker: ellis
r7_enter1.text: The glass, the clock, and no Queen.

r7_enter2.speaker: cat
r7_enter2.text: She is busy being furious elsewhere. Shall we begin?

r7_disc1.speaker: ellis
r7_disc1.text: Twelve hour cards. Each press changes its neighbours too.

r7_disc2.speaker: cat
r7_disc2.text: Time is a chain. Pull one link, others follow.

r7_wrong1.speaker: knave
r7_wrong1.text: The hours are not all lit. The court objects.

r7_wrong2.speaker: cat
r7_wrong2.text: Start at hour 1. It changes only if you press 1 or 2.

r7_wrong3.speaker: cat
r7_wrong3.text: Work left to right. Fix one hour, then move on.

r7_hint.speaker: cat
r7_hint.text: Hour 1 is lit. Press 1 and see what hour 2 does.

r7_hint2.speaker: cat
r7_hint2.text: The presses are 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 11. Do not tell the Knave.

r7_right2.speaker: cat
r7_right2.text: Splendid. And now, Ellis, the part I was dreading.

end1.speaker: ellis
end1.text: Claw scratches. A curly tail. A friend with a wide smile. The word STAY.

end2.speaker: ellis
end2.text: A grin in the glass with no cat. It was always you.

end3.speaker: cat
end3.text: You found me out. I only wanted a friend who would stay.

end4.speaker: ellis
end4.text: Wonderland froze because of you, but I know why.

end5.speaker: cat
end5.text: The glass is yours to decide. I will not stop you.

gearTrain.title: The Door Gears
gearTrain.goal: Pick two gears. The door must turn once for every 12 crank turns. Tap a gear to place it. Tap a placed gear to take it back.
gearTrain.clue: Rabbit's note: the door must turn once for each twelve crank turns.

pouring.title: The Measuring Table
pouring.goal: Get exactly 6 measures in one vial, then drink. Pouring and spilling are free. Drinking the wrong amount costs Wits.
pouring.clue: Door plate: fit for six measures only.

seating.title: The Tea Table
seating.goal: Seat all six guests by the rules. Seats go clockwise from 1.
rules: The March Hare sits in the next seat, going clockwise.
The Dormouse sits straight across from the Hatter.
The White Rabbit is not next to the March Hare.
The Dodo is next to the Dormouse.
The Duchess is not next to the Dormouse.

wordLadder.title: The Chalk Ladder
wordLadder.goal: Go from TALL to TINY. Change only one letter on each rung, and make a real word that fits the clue.

rungs.clue: A square on a bathroom wall
The sea pulls it in and out

mirrorRouting.title: The Mirror Floor
mirrorRouting.goal: Tap the living mirrors (shiny ones) to flip them. Make the beam light both Grin Stones and leave through the gate on row 8.
mirrorRouting.guide: Mirror / : east goes north, north goes east, west goes south, south goes west. Mirror \ : east goes south, south goes east, west goes north, north goes west.

poemPath.title: The Rose Lawn
poemPath.goal: Follow the poem from the front row to the back row. Tap one bed per row, going up. You may step straight or one bed sideways. Never step on a guard card.
poem: Start on a rose that blushes pink.
Next, pearl-white, quick as a blink.
Then cherry red, the Queen's own pride.
Now turn to the left for a pink one beside.
Pink again, and pink once more:
The last pink rose is the Queen's front door.
poemPath.twistNote: Garden rule: LEFT is RIGHT. When the poem says left, step to the right. Start at the bottom row.

switchboard.title: The Twelve Hours
switchboard.goal: Light all twelve hour cards. Pressing a card flips it and the cards next to it. Presses are free.

choices.title: Shatter the glass and go home.
choices.summary: The glass breaks into light. Wonderland ticks once and fades. Ellis wakes at the clockmaker's bench, and the shop clock shows a faint grin.
choices.seed: A playing card falls with your name on it: "The Looking-Glass has a twin. Come before six."

choices.title: Mend the glass and stay.
choices.summary: Ellis mends the crack with brass, and time starts again. The Cat becomes the Court's clock-keeper, right at Ellis's side.
choices.seed: A playing card falls with your name on it: "The Looking-Glass has a twin. Come before six." The mended glass has a new small crack, shaped like a key.
